name: On PCIe-only GPUs that sit across NUMA nodes, TP=2 produces garbled model output through the custom all-reduce path, and the corruption is silent
symptom: 2x NVIDIA L20 (compute capability 8.9, no NVLink) where nvidia-smi topo -m reports SYS between GPU0 and GPU1 (connection traversing PCIe plus the SMP interconnect between NUMA nodes): with '--tp 2', 'The model outputs garbled text. After I add --disable-custom-all-reduce, it outputs normally.' No error, no warning, no crash - and throughput looks entirely normal, so nothing distinguishes this from a healthy deployment short of reading the text.
root_cause: The custom all-reduce path assumes peer access that holds within a coherent PCIe/NUMA domain. Across a SYS boundary the transfer crosses the CPU interconnect between sockets, and the custom kernel's synchronization assumptions do not hold there; correctness is lost while performance is unaffected. The reporter's framing is worth preserving: they state they do not know the root reason, and attribute it to instability in cross-NUMA PCIe communication specifically in custom all-reduce without full NVLink connectivity. The fix is a topology guard, not a kernel rewrite - the upstream change adds cross-NUMA detection for PCIe devices.
workaround: Check nvidia-smi topo -m before trusting a multi-GPU config. If peer GPUs show SYS, pass --disable-custom-all-reduce (or use a topology-aware placement that keeps peers within a NUMA node). Note this is an output-correctness failure, so it is only detectable by inspecting generations or scoring them - throughput and error state are both clean.
notes: Distinct from mgpu-rccl-heterogeneous-amd-gpu-archs-fail-first-collective (which aborts loudly) and from mgpu-pcie-only-multigpu-is-communication-bound (which is correct but capped): this one is silently wrong. The two PCIe-specific TP records are also distinguished by symptom - one is throughput, one is correctness - which is why they are not merged. Cross-reference the existing llama.cpp adjacent record on NUMA for the CPU-inference version of the same effect.
